selection_rule: Purposive selection of cases located via Gwendoline Alphonso (2023) plus primary published court decisions, historical archive, and opposing decisions; NOT a random sample of jurisdictions or cases.
copyright: Observed facts and paraphrases of public historical records; modern preprint interpretations attributed, not reproduced wholesale.

persons.name: Binah
persons.role: enslaved mother; legal subject of claim

facts.payment_context: proposed residuary distribution rejected in final decree

legal_rules: under a life estate and remainder, issue follows the mother to remainder beneficiary unless express exception
different terms for another enslaved woman Nan do not create a Binah exception
records.court_disposition: Rachel Covington receives Binah and her four living children claimed under the remainder gift.
records.source_locator: case pp 317–321; Gaston J. opinion; proposed division at p 317; holding at pp318–320
limits: No testimony from Binah or the children
No count of total lifetime births
No evidence of directed conception
Proposed $55 is not an individual sale price

persons.name: Anderson
persons.role: Leah's youngest already-born child named in 1843 will

persons.name: Elizabeth Nelson
persons.role: slaveholding beneficiary of Leah and Anderson

facts.maintenance_scope: Leah and her family; not isolated pregnancy cost

legal_rules: the 1843 bequest of future increase to three daughters interpreted as births within testator's lifetime
children born after the testator's death passed with Leah to Elizabeth
the court balanced the future value of children against expenses of gestation and care
records.court_disposition: Elizabeth Nelson awarded Leah's three post-death children, not divided among her sisters.
records.source_locator: pp409–418; three children at 412; maintenance at 416; construction pp417–418
limits: Maintenance cost not exclusively attributed to prenatal or childbirth events
Three children is not an annual fertility rate
No statement from Leah or her children
Do not treat imagined profit as realized sale value

persons.name: Ann Smith
persons.role: life tenant who executed manumission deed

persons.name: Nancy Smith
persons.role: slaveholding claimant whose asserted title rejected

legal_rules: maternal status decides free/slave status of newborn, not identity of the owner
Delaware distinguished ownership of children under life tenancy from the North Carolina remainder rule
manumission deed of Ann Smith governed Stephen once court classified owner
records.court_disposition: Court ordered Stephen's freedom; Nancy's asserted title rejected under both factual alternatives.
limits: Outcome is freedom of petitioner Stephen, not abolition of hereditary slavery
Hessy's agency/consent unrecorded
The case expressly notes different rules across states

facts.mother_release: Lytha entitled to freedom upon Margaret's death, having reached 21

legal_rules: prospective conditional emancipation distinct from already-effective emancipation whose enjoyment is deferred
children followed enslaved status of mother when born
no remainder interest existed; widow's lifetime estate carried property claim to children
records.court_disposition: Mother Lytha free upon widow's death; her seven children remained legally enslaved and claimed by Margaret Johnson's estate, not by their mother.
records.source_locator: 47 Ky. 470–474, 470–471 family status, 472–474 ownership and reversal
limits: Do not imply children were granted freedom
Individual children unnamed in available opinion
No evidence of directed pairing or maternal consent

facts.reproductive_preference: raising a child every two years worth more to owner than mother's labor production
facts.recipient_policy: instruct overseers to prioritize infant care and survival for owner return

records.source_locator: Lehigh transcription item 63; Monticello page footnote10; letter dated 1819-01-17

No verified evidence of actual implementation
No named compelled conception
No generalizable mortality rate

records.case: Thomas Jefferson to John Wayles Eppes

facts.valuation_preference: woman who bears future child every two years yields capital addition, as against men's labor output
facts.debt_and_kinship_context: estate debts and intended family property transfer

records.source_locator: Letter June 30, 1820: paragraphs after description of Nicholas debt before Bedford land paragraph
limits: Proposed 20 is not known completed sale without receipt
No named pregnancy or coerced conception documented

forbidden_inferences: fourteen independent children as representative sample

evidence_evaluation.source_material: Historical court and enslaver accounts are themselves instruments of unequal power; they report ownership claims rather than captive persons' complete lives.
evidence_evaluation.counterevidence: Smith v Milman explicitly separates maternal inherited status from ownership, and orders Stephen free under an existing manumission deed; rules varied across jurisdictions.
evidence_evaluation.secondary_nexis_statistic: Alphonso's report of 212 retrieved cases and nearly 80% in 1830–60 is an UNREPLICATED NexisUNI keyword-search result, not our case-level census.
